content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells are large pasta shells filled with a creamy cheese mixture, often seasoned with herbs and spices. This version is served without tomato sauce, allowing the delicate flavor of the cheese and the texture of the pasta to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of stuffing pasta with cheese originated in Italy, where such dishes are called “conchiglie”.
The shell shape makes it easy to hold the filling without it spilling out.
The dish is often baked with a cheese topping, but without sauce the taste remains lighter and more buttery.
Cheese fillings can include ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan, and fresh herbs like basil or parsley.
Skipping the sauce reduces cooking time because the dish does not need a long simmer.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese filling is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Dairy cheese provides complete protein needed for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in dairy helps the body absorb calcium more efficiently.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: If fermented cheese is used, it can supply beneficial probiotic bacteria.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Without tomato sauce the dish contains minimal simple sugars, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheese filling may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to milk proteins.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Creamy cheeses contain saturated fats; those monitoring cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheeses are often salty; people with high blood pressure should choose low‑salt varieties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the shells hot, straight from the oven or slightly cooled. They are easy to eat with a fork or spoon, cutting the shell in half if desired. Finish with fresh herbs, a drizzle of olive oil, or a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked shells in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. Uncooked shells should be stored in a cool, dry place, while the cheese filling stays refrigerated. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months and reheated in the oven.
